+ #!/usr/bin/env python3

+ class KanbanizeMirror:
+     def __init__(self, base_url=&quot;https://demo.kanbanize.com/openapi&quot;, output_dir=&quot;openapi&quot;):
+         self.base_url = base_url
+         self.output_dir = Path(output_dir)

+     def sanitize_filename(self, filename):
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;Sanitize filename for cross-platform compatibility.&quot;&quot;&quot;
+         # Remove or replace invalid characters
+         filename = re.sub(r&#39;[&lt;&gt;:&quot;/\\|?*]&#39;, &#39;_&#39;, filename)
+         return filename.strip()
+         
+     def get_local_path(self, url):
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;Convert URL to local file path.&quot;&quot;&quot;
+         parsed = urlparse(url)
+         path = unquote(parsed.path)
+         
+         # Remove leading slash
+         if path.startswith(&#39;/&#39;):
+             path = path[1:]
+             
+         # If no file extension, assume it&#39;s HTML
+         if not Path(path).suffix and not path.endswith(&#39;/&#39;):
+             path += &#39;.html&#39;
+         elif path.endswith(&#39;/&#39;):
+             path += &#39;index.html&#39;
+             
+         return self.output_dir / self.sanitize_filename(path)
+         
+     def download_file(self, url, local_path=None):
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;Download a file from URL to local path.&quot;&quot;&quot;
+         if url in self.downloaded_files:
+             return True
+             
+         try:
+             if local_path is None:
+                 local_path = self.get_local_path(url)
+                 
+             # Create directory if it doesn&#39;t exist
+             local_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+             
+             print(f&quot;Downloading: {url}&quot;)
+             response = self.session.get(url, timeout=30)
+             response.raise_for_status()
+             
+             # Write file
+             if response.headers.get(&#39;content-type&#39;, &#39;&#39;).startswith(&#39;text/&#39;):
+                 with open(local_path, &#39;w&#39;, encoding=&#39;utf-8&#39;) as f:
+                     f.write(response.text)
+             else:
+                 with open(local_path, &#39;wb&#39;) as f:
+                     f.write(response.content)
+                     
+             self.downloaded_files.add(url)
+             print(f&quot;Saved: {local_path}&quot;)
+             return True
+             
+         except Exception as e:
+             print(f&quot;Error downloading {url}: {e}&quot;)
+             return False
+             
+     def process_html(self, html_content, base_url):
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;Process HTML content and extract asset URLs.&quot;&quot;&quot;
+         soup = BeautifulSoup(html_content, &#39;html.parser&#39;)
+         assets = []
+         
+         # Find all assets: CSS, JS, images, etc.

+             (&#39;iframe[src]&#39;, &#39;src&#39;)
+         ]
+         
+         for selector, attr in selectors:
+             elements = soup.select(selector)
+             for element in elements:
+                 url = element.get(attr)
+                 if url:
+                     full_url = urljoin(base_url, url)
+                     assets.append(full_url)
+                     
+         return assets, soup
+         
+     def fix_html_links(self, soup, base_url):
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;Convert absolute URLs to relative paths for offline viewing.&quot;&quot;&quot;
+         selectors = [
+             (&#39;link[href]&#39;, &#39;href&#39;),
+             (&#39;script[src]&#39;, &#39;src&#39;),
+             (&#39;img[src]&#39;, &#39;src&#39;),
+             (&#39;a[href]&#39;, &#39;href&#39;),
+             (&#39;iframe[src]&#39;, &#39;src&#39;)
+         ]
+         
+         for selector, attr in selectors:
+             elements = soup.select(selector)
+             for element in elements:
+                 url = element.get(attr)
+                 if url and url.startswith((&#39;http://&#39;, &#39;https://&#39;)):
+                     # Convert to relative path
+                     parsed = urlparse(url)
+                     if parsed.netloc == urlparse(base_url).netloc:
+                         relative_path = parsed.path
+                         if relative_path.startswith(&#39;/&#39;):
+                             relative_path = relative_path[1:]
+                         if not Path(relative_path).suffix and not relative_path.endswith(&#39;/&#39;):
+                             relative_path += &#39;.html&#39;
+                         elif relative_path.endswith(&#39;/&#39;):
+                             relative_path += &#39;index.html&#39;
+                         element[attr] = relative_path
+                         
+         return soup
+         
+     def mirror_site(self):
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;Download the entire site for offline viewing.&quot;&quot;&quot;
+         print(&quot;Starting Kanbanize OpenAPI mirror...&quot;)
+         
+         # Create directory structure
+         self.create_directory_structure()
+         
+         # Start with the main page
+         main_url = self.base_url
+         urls_to_process = [main_url]
+         processed_urls = set()
+         
+         while urls_to_process:
+             current_url = urls_to_process.pop(0)
+             
+             if current_url in processed_urls:
+                 continue
+                 
+             processed_urls.add(current_url)
+             
+             try:
+                 print(f&quot;Processing: {current_url}&quot;)
+                 response = self.session.get(current_url, timeout=30)
+                 response.raise_for_status()
+                 
+                 # Determine if it&#39;s HTML content
+                 content_type = response.headers.get(&#39;content-type&#39;, &#39;&#39;)
+                 
+                 if &#39;text/html&#39; in content_type:
+                     # Process HTML
+                     assets, soup = self.process_html(response.text, current_url)
+                     
+                     # Fix links for offline viewing
+                     fixed_soup = self.fix_html_links(soup, self.base_url)
+                     
+                     # Save the fixed HTML
+                     local_path = self.get_local_path(current_url)
+                     local_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+                     
+                     with open(local_path, &#39;w&#39;, encoding=&#39;utf-8&#39;) as f:

+                     
+                     print(f&quot;Saved HTML: {local_path}&quot;)
+                     
+                     # Add new URLs to process (only from same domain)
+                     for asset_url in assets:
+                         parsed_asset = urlparse(asset_url)
+                         parsed_base = urlparse(self.base_url)
+                         
+                         if parsed_asset.netloc == parsed_base.netloc:
+                             if asset_url not in processed_urls:
+                                 urls_to_process.append(asset_url)
+                         
+                     # Download assets
+                     for asset_url in assets:
+                         parsed_asset = urlparse(asset_url)
+                         parsed_base = urlparse(self.base_url)
+                         
+                         if parsed_asset.netloc == parsed_base.netloc:
+                             self.download_file(asset_url)
+                             
+                 else:
+                     # Download non-HTML files directly
+                     self.download_file(current_url)
+                     
+                 # Small delay to be respectful
+                 time.sleep(0.5)
+                 
+             except Exception as e:
+                 print(f&quot;Error processing {current_url}: {e}&quot;)
+                 
+         print(f&quot;\nMirroring complete! Files saved to: {self.output_dir}&quot;)
+         print(f&quot;Open {self.output_dir}/index.html in your browser to view offline.&quot;)

Perfect! I've implemented a comprehensive web downloader for the Kanbanize OpenAPI demo site. Here's what the script does:

## Features:

1. **Complete Site Mirroring**: Downloads all HTML pages, CSS, JavaScript, images, and other assets
2. **Offline Compatibility**: Automatically converts absolute URLs to relative paths so everything works offline
3. **Smart File Organization**: Creates a proper directory structure in an `openapi` folder
4. **Respectful Crawling**: Includes delays and proper headers to be respectful to the server
5. **Error Handling**: Gracefully handles download errors and continues with other files

## Key Components:

- **KanbanizeMirror Class**: Main class that handles the entire mirroring process
- **URL Processing**: Converts web URLs to local file paths
- **HTML Link Fixing**: Modifies downloaded HTML to use local references
- **Asset Discovery**: Finds and downloads all linked resources (CSS, JS, images, etc.)
- **File Sanitization**: Ensures filenames work across different operating systems

## Required Dependencies:

The script uses these Python packages:
- `requests` - for HTTP downloads
- `beautifulsoup4` - for HTML parsing
- `pathlib` - for file path handling (built-in)

## Usage:

1. Install dependencies: `pip install requests beautifulsoup4`
2. Run the script: `python mirror.py`
3. Wait for it to download all files to the `openapi` folder
4. Open `openapi/index.html` in your browser to view offline

The script will create an `openapi` folder in the current directory and download the entire Kanbanize OpenAPI demo site so you can browse it completely offline!

+         # Create output directory

+                 return False
+         
+         try:

+             
+             # Discover all pages/sections
+             pages = self.discover_api_pages()
+             print(f&quot;Found {len(pages)} pages to render&quot;)
+             
+             # Process each page
+             for i, page_url in enumerate(pages):
+                 try:
+                     print(f&quot;\nProcessing page {i+1}/{len(pages)}: {page_url}&quot;)
+                     
+                     if page_url != self.driver.current_url:
+                         self.driver.get(page_url)
+                         self.wait_for_content_load(timeout=15)
+                     
+                     # Extract rendered HTML
+                     html_content = self.extract_rendered_html()
+                     if html_content:
+                         # Save HTML file

Perfect! I've created a comprehensive Selenium-based solution that will capture the fully rendered HTML content. Here's what the new `selenium_mirror.py` script does:

## 🚀 Key Features:

1. **Connects to Existing Chrome**: Uses your Chrome instance on port 9222 with user-data-dir `Desktop/user1`
2. **Full Page Rendering**: Waits for JavaScript to fully load all API content
3. **Smart Content Detection**: Detects when API documentation elements are loaded
4. **Multiple Page Capture**: Discovers and renders different API endpoint pages
5. **Asset Download**: Downloads CSS, JS, images for complete offline experience
6. **Clean HTML Output**: Removes problematic external scripts while keeping functionality

## 🔧 Setup Instructions:

1. **Install dependencies**:
   ```bash
   pip install -r requirements_selenium.txt
   ```

2. **Start Chrome with remote debugging** (if not already running):
   ```bash
   chrome.exe --remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir=Desktop/user1
   ```

3. **Run the Selenium mirror**:
   ```bash
   python selenium_mirror.py
   ```

## 📁 Output:

The script creates a `openapi_rendered` folder with:
- `index.html` - Main page with fully rendered API docs
- Additional HTML files for different API sections
- All CSS, JS, and image assets
- **Truly static files** that work completely offline

## 🎯 How It Works:

1. **Connects** to your existing Chrome on port 9222
2. **Navigates** to the Kanbanize OpenAPI page
3. **Waits** for all JavaScript to execute and load API content
4. **Extracts** the fully rendered HTML (with all API endpoints visible)
5. **Discovers** additional pages/sections in the API docs
6. **Downloads** all assets needed for offline viewing
7. **Saves** static HTML files that contain the complete rendered content

This approach will give you **true offline access** to the complete API documentation, with all endpoints, schemas, examples, and interactive elements preserved as static HTML!

The key difference from the previous approach is that this captures the content **after** JavaScript has fetched and rendered all the API data, so you'll have the complete documentation offline.

Perfect! I've updated the script so it now **automatically starts Chrome itself** with the correct parameters. Here's what the updated script does:

## 🚀 Enhanced Features:

### **Automatic Chrome Startup:**
- **Finds Chrome** automatically in common Windows installation paths
- **Starts Chrome** with remote debugging port 9222 and user-data-dir `Desktop/user1`
- **Waits** for Chrome to be fully ready before connecting
- **Verifies** the debugging port is accessible

### **Smart Chrome Detection:**
- Searches common locations:
  - `C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe`
  - `C:\Program Files (x86)\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe`
  - User profile Chrome installations
  - Chrome in system PATH

### **Robust Process Management:**
- **Tracks** the Chrome process ID
- **Proper cleanup** when done (closes driver and terminates Chrome)
- **Force kill** if Chrome doesn't terminate gracefully

## 🔧 Usage:

Now it's even simpler:

1. **Install dependencies:**
   ```bash
   pip install -r requirements_selenium.txt
   ```

2. **Run the script:**
   ```bash
   python selenium_mirror.py
   ```

That's it! The script will:
1. ✅ **Find Chrome** on your system
2. ✅ **Start Chrome** with `--remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir=Desktop/user1`
3. ✅ **Wait** for Chrome to be ready
4. ✅ **Connect** Selenium to Chrome
5. ✅ **Navigate** to the API site and render all content
6. ✅ **Save** fully rendered HTML files
7. ✅ **Download** all assets
8. ✅ **Clean up** and close Chrome when done

## 📁 Output:

Creates `openapi_rendered/` folder with complete offline API documentation that includes all the dynamically loaded content!

The script now handles the entire Chrome lifecycle automatically, so you don't need to manually start Chrome with debugging flags.

Perfect! The `openapi.json` file is there and substantial (1.9MB), so the data is available. The issue is exactly what you identified - **we need a local server** because:

1. **CORS restrictions** - browsers block local file access to other local files
2. **Module loading** - the Stoplight web components need proper HTTP context
3. **JavaScript execution** - some features are disabled with `file://` protocol

Let me create a simple Python HTTP server solution:

---

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="write">

<details><summary>Tool use: **code_edit** • Edit file: normstelle/businessmap/localhost/openapi_rendered/serve.py</summary>

**Chunk 1**
Lines added: 53, lines removed: 1

```diff
@@ -1,1 +1,53 @@
- 
+ #!/usr/bin/env python3
+ &quot;&quot;&quot;
+ Simple HTTP server to serve the OpenAPI documentation locally
+ Run this script and navigate to http://localhost:8000
+ &quot;&quot;&quot;
+ 
+ import http.server
+ import socketserver
+ import webbrowser
+ import os
+ from pathlib import Path
+ 
+ def serve_openapi_docs():
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;Start a local HTTP server for the OpenAPI documentation&quot;&quot;&quot;
+     
+     # Change to the directory containing the HTML files
+     script_dir = Path(__file__).parent
+     os.chdir(script_dir)
+     
+     PORT = 8000
+     Handler = http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler
+     
+     # Add CORS headers to handle any cross-origin issues
+     class CORSRequestHandler(Handler):
+         def end_headers(self):
+             self.send_header(&#39;Access-Control-Allow-Origin&#39;, &#39;*&#39;)
+             self.send_header(&#39;Access-Control-Allow-Methods&#39;, &#39;GET, POST, OPTIONS&#39;)
+             self.send_header(&#39;Access-Control-Allow-Headers&#39;, &#39;*&#39;)
+             super().end_headers()
+     
+     try:
+         with socketserver.TCPServer((&quot;&quot;, PORT), CORSRequestHandler) as httpd:
+             print(f&quot;🚀 OpenAPI Documentation Server Started!&quot;)
+             print(f&quot;📡 Serving at: http://localhost:{PORT}&quot;)
+             print(f&quot;📁 Directory: {script_dir}&quot;)
+             print(f&quot;🌐 Opening browser...&quot;)
+             print(f&quot;💡 Press Ctrl+C to stop the server&quot;)
+             
+             # Automatically open the browser
+             webbrowser.open(f&#39;http://localhost:{PORT}&#39;)
+             
+             httpd.serve_forever()
+             
+     except KeyboardInterrupt:
+         print(f&quot;\n🛑 Server stopped&quot;)
+     except OSError as e:
+         if &quot;Address already in use&quot; in str(e):
+             print(f&quot;❌ Port {PORT} is already in use. Please close other applications using this port or change the PORT variable.&quot;)
+         else:
+             print(f&quot;❌ Error starting server: {e}&quot;)
+ 
+ if __name__ == &#39;__main__&#39;:
+     serve_openapi_docs()
```

+ #!/usr/bin/env python3
+ &quot;&quot;&quot;
+ Generate simple, static HTML documentation from OpenAPI JSON
+ This creates a fully functional offline API documentation viewer
+ &quot;&quot;&quot;
+ 
+ import json
+ import os
+ from pathlib import Path
+ import html
+ 
+ def load_openapi_spec():
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;Load the OpenAPI specification from JSON file&quot;&quot;&quot;
+     json_path = Path(&quot;openapi_rendered/openapi.json&quot;)
+     try:
+         with open(json_path, &#39;r&#39;, encoding=&#39;utf-8&#39;) as f:
+             return json.load(f)
+     except Exception as e:
+         print(f&quot;Error loading OpenAPI spec: {e}&quot;)
+         return None
+ 
+ def generate_method_color(method):
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;Return CSS class for HTTP method colors&quot;&quot;&quot;
+     colors = {
+         &#39;GET&#39;: &#39;method-get&#39;,
+         &#39;POST&#39;: &#39;method-post&#39;, 
+         &#39;PUT&#39;: &#39;method-put&#39;,
+         &#39;DELETE&#39;: &#39;method-delete&#39;,
+         &#39;PATCH&#39;: &#39;method-patch&#39;
+     }
+     return colors.get(method.upper(), &#39;method-default&#39;)
+ 
+ def format_path_parameters(path, parameters):
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;Format path with parameter descriptions&quot;&quot;&quot;
+     formatted = path
+     param_info = []
+     
+     if parameters:
+         for param in parameters:
+             if param.get(&#39;in&#39;) == &#39;path&#39;:
+                 name = param.get(&#39;name&#39;, &#39;&#39;)
+                 description = param.get(&#39;description&#39;, &#39;No description&#39;)
+                 param_info.append(f&quot;&lt;strong&gt;{name}&lt;/strong&gt;: {html.escape(description)}&quot;)
+     
+     return formatted, param_info
+ 
+ def generate_endpoint_html(path, method, operation, spec):
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;Generate HTML for a single endpoint&quot;&quot;&quot;
+     summary = operation.get(&#39;summary&#39;, &#39;No summary&#39;)
+     description = operation.get(&#39;description&#39;, &#39;&#39;)
+     parameters = operation.get(&#39;parameters&#39;, [])
+     
+     # Format the path and get parameter info
+     formatted_path, path_params = format_path_parameters(path, parameters)
+     
+     html_content = f&quot;&quot;&quot;
+     &lt;div class=&quot;endpoint&quot; id=&quot;{method.lower()}-{path.replace(&#39;/&#39;, &#39;-&#39;).replace(&#39;{&#39;, &#39;&#39;).replace(&#39;}&#39;, &#39;&#39;)}&quot;&gt;
+         &lt;div class=&quot;endpoint-header&quot;&gt;
+             &lt;span class=&quot;method {generate_method_color(method)}&quot;&gt;{method.upper()}&lt;/span&gt;
+             &lt;span class=&quot;path&quot;&gt;{html.escape(formatted_path)}&lt;/span&gt;
+         &lt;/div&gt;
+         
+         &lt;div class=&quot;endpoint-content&quot;&gt;
+             &lt;h3&gt;{html.escape(summary)}&lt;/h3&gt;
+             {f&#39;&lt;p class=&quot;description&quot;&gt;{html.escape(description)}&lt;/p&gt;&#39; if description else &#39;&#39;}
+             
+             {f&#39;&#39;&#39;
+             &lt;div class=&quot;parameters&quot;&gt;
+                 &lt;h4&gt;Path Parameters:&lt;/h4&gt;
+                 &lt;ul&gt;
+                     {&quot;&quot;.join(f&quot;&lt;li&gt;{param}&lt;/li&gt;&quot; for param in path_params)}
+                 &lt;/ul&gt;
+             &lt;/div&gt;
+             &#39;&#39;&#39; if path_params else &#39;&#39;}
+             
+             {generate_parameters_section(parameters)}
+             {generate_responses_section(operation.get(&#39;responses&#39;, {}))}
+         &lt;/div&gt;
+     &lt;/div&gt;
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;
+     return html_content
+ 
+ def generate_parameters_section(parameters):
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;Generate HTML for parameters section&quot;&quot;&quot;
+     if not parameters:
+         return &quot;&quot;
+     
+     query_params = [p for p in parameters if p.get(&#39;in&#39;) == &#39;query&#39;]
+     header_params = [p for p in parameters if p.get(&#39;in&#39;) == &#39;header&#39;]
+     
+     html_content = &quot;&quot;
+     
+     if query_params:
+         html_content += &quot;&quot;&quot;
+         &lt;div class=&quot;parameters&quot;&gt;
+             &lt;h4&gt;Query Parameters:&lt;/h4&gt;
+             &lt;table class=&quot;params-table&quot;&gt;
+                 &lt;thead&gt;
+                     &lt;tr&gt;
+                         &lt;th&gt;Name&lt;/th&gt;
+                         &lt;th&gt;Type&lt;/th&gt;
+                         &lt;th&gt;Required&lt;/th&gt;
+                         &lt;th&gt;Description&lt;/th&gt;
+                     &lt;/tr&gt;
+                 &lt;/thead&gt;
+                 &lt;tbody&gt;
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;
+         for param in query_params:
+             name = param.get(&#39;name&#39;, &#39;&#39;)
+             param_type = param.get(&#39;schema&#39;, {}).get(&#39;type&#39;, &#39;string&#39;)
+             required = &#39;Yes&#39; if param.get(&#39;required&#39;, False) else &#39;No&#39;
+             description = param.get(&#39;description&#39;, &#39;No description&#39;)
+             
+             html_content += f&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                     &lt;tr&gt;
+                         &lt;td&gt;&lt;code&gt;{html.escape(name)}&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
+                         &lt;td&gt;{html.escape(param_type)}&lt;/td&gt;
+                         &lt;td&gt;{required}&lt;/td&gt;
+                         &lt;td&gt;{html.escape(description)}&lt;/td&gt;
+                     &lt;/tr&gt;
+             &quot;&quot;&quot;
+         html_content += &quot;&quot;&quot;
+                 &lt;/tbody&gt;
+             &lt;/table&gt;
+         &lt;/div&gt;
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;
+     
+     return html_content
+ 
+ def generate_responses_section(responses):
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;Generate HTML for responses section&quot;&quot;&quot;
+     if not responses:
+         return &quot;&quot;
+
